# Dungeons & Dolphins roadmap

This roadmap contains user-facing features and improvements that are not present in version 4.19. Each planned build contains eight features with full descriptions of what the feature would do and how it would improve play. Existing capabilities are documented in `README.md` and `FEATURE_CHECKLIST.md` instead of being repeated here.

## 4.19.1 — Faster play at the table

1. **Quick Rolls:** Add a character-driven roll screen for ability checks, saving throws and skills using the active character's current modifiers. Normal, Advantage, Disadvantage and Guidance controls would make common rolls available without manually translating a sheet value into the general Dice Roller.
2. **Grant Review Center:** Add a normal Character-menu entry for viewing pending, skipped and custom progression grants without first reaching the existing review workflow through a grant problem. This would make retry, skip and edit actions discoverable and give players one place to inspect unresolved progression work.
3. **Concentration Helper:** Let the player enter damage taken and immediately roll the required Constitution save against the calculated concentration DC using the character's current save modifier. This would remove repeated DC arithmetic during combat while leaving concentration state under the player's control.
4. **Combat Quick Bar:** Add a compact screen containing favorite weapon attacks, favorite spell attacks, HP/temp HP, reaction state and the most important combat resources. This would reduce repeated navigation through the full Combat menu during every turn.
5. **Ammo Stack Choice:** When several Inventory stacks satisfy a weapon's ammunition token, show the matching stacks and let the player choose which one to consume. Specialty ammunition such as Fire Arrows, Silvered Arrows or named bolt types could then be selected intentionally instead of relying on the first eligible stack.
6. **Rest Preview:** Show the resources a Short Rest or Long Rest is about to recover before applying the rest. This would make Hit Dice, spell-resource and Feature recharge effects clear before character state changes.
7. **Reaction Turn Sync:** When the active character reaches the start of its turn in Initiative, optionally set Reaction back to Ready while retaining the manual Reaction toggle. This would reduce combat bookkeeping and better connect DNDolphins combat state to the turn tracker.
8. **Character Summary Card:** Add one condensed screen for AC, HP, speed, proficiency bonus, initiative, passive scores, Spell Attack/DC, Hit Dice and important remaining resources. It would provide a fast at-a-glance character sheet when full editing is unnecessary.

## 4.19.2 — Inventory, Spellbook and Feature organization

1. **Inventory Search and Sorting:** Add owned-Item search plus sorting by name, category, equipped state, quantity, container or weight while retaining bounded paging. Larger inventories would become much faster to navigate without requiring the whole sidecar to remain resident.
2. **Container Browsing:** Let a container open as a focused Inventory view containing only the Items assigned to it, with quick move-in and move-out actions. Bags, pouches and chests would become practical navigation tools instead of only stored container references.
3. **Equipment Loadouts:** Allow a small number of named equipped-item sets such as Travel, Dungeon, Ranged or Social. Switching a loadout would change equipped state in one action while preserving Item records, quantities and containers.
4. **Spellbook Search:** Add name search to the owned Spellbook and Add Spell catalog alongside the existing level, class, ritual, school, source, status and eligibility filters. Finding one spell in a large known/prepared list would require far less paging.
5. **Spell Favorites / Quick-Cast List:** Let players mark frequently used spells as favorites and open them from a compact combat-oriented list. Favorites would be a navigation layer only and would not alter Known, Prepared, Always Prepared or free-cast state.
6. **Feature Favorites:** Let frequently used Features and limited-use resources appear in a compact favorites list. Abilities such as Action Surge, Second Wind or Channel Divinity would be reachable without paging through every Feature.
7. **Item Favorites / Quick-Use List:** Let frequently referenced or consumable Items be marked as favorites and opened from a short list. Potions, ammunition variants, tools and other often-used gear would become faster to find while keeping the underlying Inventory record unchanged.
8. **Character-to-Character Transfer:** Allow Inventory Items or currency to be safely moved or copied between local characters. Party loot sharing and equipment handoffs would no longer require manually recreating the same record in another profile.

## 4.19.3 — Initiative and GM workflow

1. **Monster Turn Tools:** From Initiative, allow a Bestiary participant to open its stat block and roll common attacks/damage without leaving the encounter workflow. Initiative could then serve as a lightweight GM combat console rather than only turn-order and HP tracking.
2. **Encounter Round Notes:** Allow a short note or marker on the current encounter or round for lair actions, reinforcements, environmental hazards or scripted events. Time-sensitive reminders would stay beside the turn order instead of requiring a separate Journal entry.
3. **Encounter Group Inserts:** Allow a saved group such as guards, a patrol or a boss/minion package to be inserted into another encounter or an active Initiative setup. Saved Encounters already preserve complete encounters; group inserts would provide reusable components inside a different encounter.
4. **Initiative Condition Duration:** Optionally attach a round or turn duration to a participant condition and decrement it as turns advance. Short-lived effects could expire automatically while ordinary free-form conditions remain manually controlled.
5. **Encounter Loot Packages:** Let a Bestiary or Initiative encounter carry an optional reward package of Items and currency that can be awarded to the active character after combat. This would connect GM encounter preparation to Inventory bookkeeping without changing Adventure's existing direct Item-reward behavior.
6. **Combat History Browser:** Add an Initiative screen for browsing the completed-encounter history records already saved through explicit End + Save History. Players and GMs could review encounter date, rounds, party state and surviving opponents directly on the Flipper.
7. **Party Damage / Healing Actions:** Allow one damage or healing amount to be applied to several selected Initiative participants in a single action. Area effects, mass healing and environmental damage would require less repetitive HP editing while each participant would retain its own final HP.
8. **Reinforcement Waves:** Let an encounter pre-stage monsters or NPCs to enter combat at a chosen round or on manual confirmation. GMs could prepare ambushes and multi-phase fights without rebuilding the roster mid-combat.

## 4.19.4 — Adventure and Journal quality-of-life

1. **Adventure Bookmarks and Favorites:** Allow campaigns or specific scenes to be marked for quick access, with a short recent-campaign list. Returning to frequently played campaigns or useful scenes would be faster than browsing the full campaign list each time.
2. **Adventure Recap:** Add a compact summary of the active campaign, current scene, recent major choices and unresolved objectives. Players returning after a long break could regain context without rereading every previous scene.
3. **Campaign Progress Viewer:** Expose the active campaign's recorded quest flags, achievements, checkpoints and completed milestone/reward markers in a readable progress screen. Adventure already uses that state internally for branching and one-shot rewards; this would make the character's progress understandable to the player.
4. **Journal Search and Filters:** Add text search and filters for category, completion state, date range and milestone/item entries. The Journal would remain useful as a long-term campaign record even after it contains many sessions of notes.
5. **Journal Reference Links:** Allow a Journal entry to store optional links to an owned Item, Spell, Feature, Bestiary monster or saved encounter and open that referenced record directly. This would extend the current specific Milestone/Inventory actions into a general cross-reference system.
6. **Session Log Helper:** Add a structured Journal template with date, party state, milestones, important NPCs/monsters, loot and free-form notes. It would make consistent session summaries quick to create while ordinary free-form entries remain available.
7. **Campaign Reward Preview:** Show upcoming explicit campaign rewards and selectable reward choices before they are committed to character state. Item, spell and other reward application would be easier to review when a campaign scene offers several outcomes.
8. **Scene Annotations:** Let a player attach a personal note to the current Adventure scene without modifying the campaign pack itself. Players could record theories, reminders, NPC details or table rulings exactly where they become relevant and revisit them later.

## 4.19.5 — Rules, customization and extensibility

1. **Ruleset Profiles:** Allow an optional per-character ruleset selection when materially different compatible rule families cannot be derived safely from existing character data. This would support multiple D&D-era or rules variants without mixing incompatible calculations inside one character.
2. **Custom Progression Packs:** Support documented external metadata for homebrew classes, subclasses, species, backgrounds, level choices and deterministic grants without recompiling the FAP. The parser would retain bounded streaming so custom progression content does not require loading an entire pack into memory.
3. **External Spell and Item Catalogs:** Allow optional user-supplied Spell and Item catalog files to be merged with the bundled catalogs using documented row formats. Homebrew content could appear in the same filtered pickers without replacing built-in SRD entries or manually typing every record.
4. **Pack Library and Controls:** Add a reliable user-facing screen for discovering installed campaign and monster packs and enabling, disabling or inspecting them without editing files manually. It would build on the existing pack formats while keeping normal Adventure and Bestiary menus focused on play rather than diagnostics.
5. **User-Defined Quick Actions:** Let each character choose a small set of Home shortcuts tailored to how that character is played. A martial character could prioritize weapon attacks and Features while a caster could prioritize Spellbook, Concentration and spell resources.
6. **Exportable Session Summary:** Generate a compact text summary containing selected character state, recent Journal/session information and encounter results. The summary could be archived or shared outside the Flipper without exposing unrelated save internals.
7. **Rules Reference Cards:** Add an offline quick-reference browser for common combat actions, conditions, rest rules, concentration, cover and other frequently checked table rules. It would reduce dependence on an external rulebook for routine reminders without trying to replace full source material.
8. **Campaign Pack Builder:** Add a guided editor for creating simple custom campaigns, scenes, choices and rewards using the existing campaign-pack model. Players could build or revise small adventures on-device and export them for further editing without hand-authoring every metadata row.

## 4.19.6 — Character management and progression

1. **Inspiration Roll Integration:** Let Inspiration be applied directly from character-driven roll workflows, turning the next eligible d20 roll into Advantage and optionally consuming the Inspiration mark after the roll. Inspiration already exists as character state; connecting it to actual rolls would make the resource useful at the moment it matters instead of requiring separate manual bookkeeping.
2. **Structured Training & Proficiency Sheet:** Add dedicated user-facing sections for tool proficiencies, armor training and weapon training instead of relying on one free-form Other Proficiencies field. Structured entries would make granted training easier to inspect, edit and reuse for future rules checks while still allowing custom text for homebrew proficiencies.
3. **Level Snapshot Browser & Rollback:** Expose saved pre-level character snapshots in a readable history and allow an explicit restore to a selected prior level state. This would provide a safer recovery path when a level-up, multiclass decision or progression choice was entered incorrectly without forcing the player to restore an unrelated general backup.
4. **Roleplay Profile:** Add optional character-sheet fields for personality traits, ideals, bonds, flaws, appearance and general character notes. Keeping roleplay information beside the mechanical sheet would make DNDolphins more complete at the table without affecting combat or progression calculations.
5. **Profile Search, Sort & Favorites:** Add search and sorting for local characters by name, class and level, plus a small Favorites list for frequently used profiles. Players who keep campaign variants, NPC sheets or several party characters would be able to switch profiles without paging through an increasingly long creation-order list.
6. **Export & Archive Browser:** Replace the current first-export import workflow with a browser for available exports and archived character sets, including explicit import, restore and delete actions. This would make backups and archived characters manageable on-device instead of depending on filename order or external storage editing.
7. **Progression History:** Add a per-character timeline showing completed ASI/Feat choices, deterministic grants, milestone levels and other recorded progression decisions by character/class level. The app already stores enough progression identity to prevent many duplicate grants; presenting that history would help players understand how the current build was assembled and spot an accidental choice more easily.
8. **Multiclass Level Planner:** Let a player preview one or more hypothetical future class levels without changing the saved character. The planner could show projected proficiency bonus, Hit Dice, fixed-average HP gain, spell-slot progression, cantrip/prepared limits and upcoming ASI/Feat choices so multiclass decisions can be evaluated before committing them.

## 4.19.7 — Combat automation and tactical tracking

1. **Damage Intake Assistant:** Let the player enter incoming damage, select a damage type and have the app apply temporary HP first while showing relevant resistance, immunity or vulnerability adjustments before changing HP. This would reduce arithmetic during combat while keeping the final damage application explicit and reviewable.
2. **Death Save Roller:** Add a dedicated death-save action that rolls the d20, records a success or failure, handles natural 1/natural 20 outcomes, and clearly reports when the character stabilizes or dies. The existing success/failure counters would remain editable, but routine death-save rounds would no longer require a separate Dice Roller and manual counter update.
3. **Condition Library & Quick Apply:** Provide a compact library of standard conditions with short descriptions and a quick toggle/apply interface while retaining free-form Conditions text for custom effects. This would make common states such as Prone, Grappled, Restrained or Poisoned faster to record and easier to interpret during play.
4. **Action Economy Tracker:** Add optional Action, Bonus Action, Movement and Reaction availability to the combat view and reset the appropriate resources when the character's turn begins. Players who want stricter turn bookkeeping could see at a glance what remains without forcing this workflow on users who prefer the current lightweight combat screen.
5. **Weapon Mastery Support:** Add an optional mastery property to supported weapons and surface its rule/effect beside Weapon Attacks when the character has access to that mastery. This would let newer rulesets represent mastery-driven weapon choices without turning every mastery into a manually remembered Feature note.
6. **Two-Weapon / Bonus Attack Helper:** Allow compatible light/off-hand weapon attacks to be paired into a turn-oriented attack flow that calculates the correct ability-damage treatment and keeps the two attacks together. Dual-wielding characters would spend less time reopening separate weapon records and remembering which modifiers apply to the follow-up attack.
7. **Recent Combat Roll Log:** Keep a small bounded history of recent weapon attacks, spell resolutions and combat-oriented dice results with their final totals and key modifiers. Players could check what just happened after the result screen is gone without rerolling or writing every attack into the Journal.
8. **Target Defense Helper:** Allow an optional target AC or saving-throw defense to be entered before an attack/spell resolution so the result can report hit/miss or success/failure instead of only the raw roll. The target value would be temporary encounter context, avoiding any requirement to create a full Bestiary or Initiative participant just to resolve one attack.

## 4.19.8 — Equipment, treasure and inventory operations

1. **Quick Use Consumables:** Add a one-action Use command for consumable Items that can decrement Stack Qty, a charge or another configured expendable value and report the remaining amount. Potions, scroll-like custom Items, ammunition bundles and limited-use gear would become practical to manage without opening the full Item Editor after every use.
2. **Item Charge Recharge Rules:** Let charged Items define a recharge cadence such as Dawn, Short Rest, Long Rest or manual, with optional fixed/die-based recovery where appropriate. Rest actions could then refresh supported equipment resources alongside Features while custom or unusual Items remain manually controlled.
3. **Item Value & Shop Calculator:** Add an optional value field for owned/catalog Items plus a lightweight buy/sell workflow that totals selected quantities, converts coin denominations and applies a price multiplier or discount before changing currency. Shopping sessions would require less mental arithmetic while merchant pricing and final transaction approval remain under the player's control.
4. **Loot Splitter:** Let a currency or Item-quantity reward be divided among selected local characters, with remainder handling shown before anything is written. Groups tracked on one Flipper could distribute treasure consistently without repeating manual currency edits across several profiles.
5. **Batch Inventory Actions:** Allow multiple Items to be selected for common operations such as Equip/Unequip, move to a container, mark carried, delete or change quantity by a shared amount. Inventory cleanup after a shopping trip, loot haul or equipment swap would take far fewer repetitive editor visits.
6. **Identification State & Hidden Notes:** Add optional Unidentified/Identified state plus player-visible and hidden-detail fields for magic or mystery Items. A GM could record the true properties of an Item without immediately exposing them in the normal Inventory view, then reveal the details when the character identifies it.
7. **Item Tags & Custom Collections:** Allow user-defined tags such as Quest, Consumable, Crafting, Camping or Sell and filter the owned Inventory by those tags. This would provide flexible organization beyond the fixed catalog categories without changing the Item's mechanical type or container.
8. **Treasure & Valuables Ledger:** Add a compact ledger for gems, art objects, trade goods and other valuables with quantity and estimated value, separate from everyday equipped gear. Valuable treasure could be tracked without cluttering the normal combat/equipment Inventory while still contributing to an optional total wealth estimate.

## 4.19.9 — Deeper spellcasting support

1. **Known / Prepared Limit Assistant:** Compare each class's current Known/Prepared counts with its calculated or configured limits and show over/under status before the player leaves Spellbook. The app would continue allowing manual exceptions, but ordinary spell-selection mistakes would become obvious before a session starts.
2. **Spell Component Metadata:** Extend Spell records with verbal, somatic and material component flags plus optional material text, value and consumed state. Players could check casting requirements from the Spellbook instead of relying entirely on Notes or an external reference.
3. **Material Component Inventory Links:** Allow a spell's material component to reference an owned Item or consumable quantity and warn when the required component is missing. Expensive or consumed components could then connect directly to Inventory bookkeeping without making ordinary component-pouch spells cumbersome.
4. **Spell Duration & Effect Tracker:** Let a cast spell start an optional duration tracker for rounds, minutes or hours and associate it with Concentration when appropriate. Active spell effects would be easier to manage across Initiative turns, while instantaneous and manually tracked spells would continue to work as they do now.
5. **Range, Area & Target Metadata:** Add structured range, target count and area-shape/size fields to Spell records and show them in the combat/casting view. This would turn the Spellbook into a more complete quick reference and give future encounter tools enough structured data to assist with targeting without parsing prose.
6. **Class Spell Learning Assistant:** Add class-aware workflows for learning, replacing or preparing spells when a class has specific progression rules, such as Wizard spellbook additions or limited known-spell replacements. The assistant would suggest legal operations and update the existing Spellbook records without automatically choosing spells for the player.
7. **Metamagic & Spell Modification Support:** Allow selected casting modifiers to alter supported spell cost, range, targeting or roll behavior while consuming a linked Feature/resource pool. Sorcerer-style metamagic and similar homebrew casting options could be represented as explicit cast-time choices instead of free-form notes.
8. **Custom Structured Spell Effects:** Extend the custom Spell editor with optional attack/save, damage, healing, scaling and secondary-effect metadata comparable to the structured information used by supported bundled spells. Homebrew spells could then participate in Spell Attacks and upcasting logic rather than being limited to name/notes/resource bookkeeping.

## 4.19.10 — Bestiary and encounter design

1. **Advanced Monster Search:** Expand Bestiary search beyond monster names to optionally match type, environment, role, traits, actions and other stat-block text. A GM looking for concepts such as `grapple`, `undead`, `swamp` or `teleport` could discover useful monsters without already knowing their names.
2. **Monster Sorting:** Add sortable Bestiary views for name, CR, XP, type, environment or role while retaining bounded streaming windows. Browsing a filtered set would become more predictable and useful for encounter preparation without loading the full catalog into memory.
3. **Manual Encounter Builder:** Add a mode where monsters can be searched and added/removed one at a time while the current XP/difficulty total updates continuously. GMs who want a specific story-driven composition could build it directly instead of repeatedly regenerating a random encounter until the desired creatures appear.
4. **Encounter Scaling Suggestions:** From a generated, saved or manually built encounter, suggest small add/remove/quantity changes that move the encounter toward Low, Moderate or High difficulty for the configured party. The suggestions would be advisory and preview their XP effect before changing the encounter.
5. **Clone Monster as Custom:** Allow any bundled or pack-provided monster to be copied into the custom-monster editor as a new independent record. Homebrew variants, weakened bosses and reskinned creatures could start from an existing stat block rather than requiring every field to be re-entered manually.
6. **Monster Recharge Tracker:** Let Initiative/Bestiary track recharge abilities such as Recharge 5–6 and roll/check them at the appropriate start-of-turn point. Monster powers would be less likely to be forgotten during long fights while free-form Actions text remains available for creatures without structured recharge abilities.
7. **Legendary & Lair Action Tracker:** Add optional legendary-action points and lair-action reminders for monsters that use them, including refresh at the appropriate round/turn boundary. Boss encounters would be easier to run without keeping a separate paper reminder for off-turn action resources.
8. **Saved Encounter Notes & Tags:** Allow saved encounters to carry short GM notes and user-defined tags such as Boss, City, Undead, Random or Campaign Name. Saved Encounters could then be organized and reused by purpose rather than relying only on the encounter's display name.
